chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The people did not become grey-haired. So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saw grey hair in his beard, so he said: 'O Lord, what is this?' He said: 'This is reverence/grace.' So he said: 'O Lord, increase me in reverence/grace.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of grey hair in Islam according to the hadith of Ibrahim?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes the theological basis for retaining grey hair as a symbol of 'waqar' (dignity and maturity), contrasting it with the practice of plucking or cutting it to appear younger. It highlights Prophet Ibrahim’s (peace be upon him) conscious choice to embrace natural signs of aging as spiritual virtues, reinforcing the scholarly view that grey hair reflects inner wisdom and reverence rather than mere physical decay. This narrative is frequently cited in fiqh discussions regarding the permissibility and merit of keeping grey hair visible as a mark of prophetic sunnah.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The people were not becoming grey-haired. So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> saw something in his<sup>as</sup> beard, so he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is this?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “This is a reverence”. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Increase the reverence for me<sup>as</sup>’’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
People did not grow gray hairs but Ibrahim ‘Alayhi al- Salam, found gray in his beard and asked, ‘O Lord, what is this?’ He said, ‘It is reverence.’ He then said, ‘O Lord, increase my reverence.’”
